title: Degauss Coil
pages: Craft the Degauss Coil with gold, copper, one bismuth ingot (forge:ingots/bismuth), Purified Salts and two Stator Coils from the Polarity Inverter. Its Degaussed Armature output unlocks the Armor Delaminator before the Electrolyzer.

Place a diamond block directly beneath it, a sea lantern directly above it, glowstone on all four horizontal sides, and copper blocks in the four horizontal corners to brace the ring. Any missing or swapped brace, side, cap or base stops operation. Right-click the formed controller with feedstock from a loaded degaussing recipe. It loads one recipe batch into its stock buffer, processes it over 40 ticks, and holds the output for empty-hand collection or bottom-face extraction. It needs no FE; hand use and the automation buffer below share the same recipes.

It runs 20 exclusive datapack degaussing recipes. Nineteen degauss workshop and utility fixtures (lectern, loom, cartography table, fletching table, smithing table, grindstone, stonecutter, bell, scaffolding, barrel, composter, jukebox, respawn anchor, brewing stand, flower pot, armor stand, item frame, glow item frame and painting) back into useful stock at a lossy ratio. Four barrels recover eight oak planks; four composters recover eight oak slabs. The twentieth fuses two Stator Coils from the Polarity Inverter into a Degaussed Armature.

The Degaussed Armature is reserved as the gate material for the next apparatus. With JEI installed, look up Degaussing or inspect the Degauss Coil catalyst to see all 20 loaded datapack recipes, input batch counts, results and formation requirements.

Automation: the controller also keeps a one-stack stock buffer and a one-stack product buffer. Hoppers, droppers and sided item pipes insert from the top and the four sides; only items that match a loaded degaussing recipe are accepted, and simulated inserts never change the buffer. While the structure is formed and owned, it runs one batch every 40 ticks (2 seconds) without power, using the same recipe priority as hand use (lowest resource ID first). Products wait in the buffer and are pulled from the bottom face, e.g. by a hopper under a Stock Hatch that replaces the base part. If the structure breaks, work pauses and progress resets; if the product buffer is full or holds a different item, work waits. Sneak-use with an empty hand on a face to cycle it between In, Out and Off; right-click with an empty hand to collect buffered products. Buffers, progress and face settings are saved with the chunk, and breaking the controller drops both buffers.

Stock Hatches: every face of this controller is covered by a frame part, so hoppers and pipes reach it through Stock Hatches. Place a hatch instead of any part that touches the controller face-to-face; at most two hatches may stand in, and a third breaks formation. A hatch relays only while the frame is formed, and it relays the controller face it covers: insert stock into a hatch on an In face, and extract products from a hatch whose face you sneak-use with an empty hand to cycle to Out (the base face starts as Out). For example, swap one side part for a hatch fed by a hopper pointing into it from beside, and swap the base part for a hatch with a hopper beneath it. A hopper touching a redstone block or other powered part is locked by vanilla rules. Right-clicking a hatch with an empty hand collects the product buffer.
